newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.N. prosecutor says tribunal shown to be fair.
newsitem.headline: U.N. prosecutor says tribunal shown to be fair.

text.p: The chief prosecutor at a U.N. war crimes tribunal said on Friday she considered that the 10-year jail sentence handed down to a Bosnian Croat was fair and appropriate.

Louise Arbour, chief prosecutor at the U.N. criminal tribunal for former Yugoslavia, told reporters she was satisfied with the sentence -- the first passed by an international war crimes tribunal for half a century.
"I'm very content with the reasoning of the court and the result of this case. It's a very important moment in the life of the tribunal and a very fair and satisfactory result," she said.

The tribunal earlier sentenced Drazen Erdemovic, a Croat who confessed to taking part in the Bosnian Serb Army (BSA) massacre of over 1,200 unarmed Moslems at Srebrenica in July 1995, to 10 years in jail.
Charged with crimes against humanity, he pleaded guilty in May to being one of the BSA's execution squad that carried out the killings after Serbs overran the U.N. "safe haven".
Arbour said that Erdemovic's guilty plea and his cooperation with prosecutors should tell victims of the 3-1/2 year Bosnian conflict that they can expect fair justice from The Hague.

"The fact that it's the result of a guilty plea is extremely significant. It is something that victims should take a lot of comfort in (knowing) that there are people who show sufficient remorse and confidence in the justice process to come forward."
Arbour said that more senior officers charged with genocide and war crimes could expect far tougher sentences.
"If and when we are successful in having them tried...the sentences they will receive will reflect their degree of culpability," she added.
"The bigger fish will be treated much more severely."
